Acidogenesis is the second stage in the four stages of [anaerobic digestion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anaerobic_digestion): * [Hydrolysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrolysis): A chemical reaction where [particulate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particulate)s are solubilized and large [polymer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymer)s converted into simpler [monomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monomer)s; * Acidogenesis: A biological reaction where simple monomers are converted into volatile [fatty acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatty_acid)s; * [Acetogenesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acetogenesis): A biological reaction where volatile fatty acids are converted into [acetic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acetic_acid), [carbon dioxide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_dioxide), and [hydrogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen) * [Methanogenesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methanogenesis): A biological reaction where [acetate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acetate)s are converted into [methane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methane) and carbon dioxide, while hydrogen is consumed.

definition: Bacterial adhesins are cell-surface components or appendages of bacteria that facilitate [adhesion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adhesion) or adherence to other cells or to surfaces, usually in the host they are infecting or living in.

bacterial capsule is a large structure common to many [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria).
Bacterial cellular morphologies are the shapes that are characteristic of various types of [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) and often key to their identification.

Bacterial circadian rhythms, like other [circadian rhythm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circadian_rhythm)s, are [endogenous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endogeny_(biology)) It is suspected that other gut bacteria may have circadian clocks, too.

Bacterial conjugation is the transfer of genetic material between [bacterial cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) by direct cell-to-cell contact or by a bridge-like connection between two cells.

Bacterial genomes are generally smaller and less varied in size between species when compared with [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome)s of [eukaryote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryote)s.

Bacterial lawn is a term used by [microbiologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiologist)s to describe the appearance of [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria)l [colonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colony_(biology)) when all the individual colonies on a [Petri dish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petri_dish) or [agar plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agar_plate) merge to form a field or mat of bacteria.

Bacterial motility is the ability of [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) to [move independently](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motility) using [metabolic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metabolic) energy.

Bacterial taxonomy is subfield of [taxonomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linnaean_taxonomy) devoted to the classification of [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) specimens into [taxonomic rank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxonomic_rank)s.

Bacteriological water analysis is a method of analysing water to estimate the numbers of [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) present and, if needed, to find out what sort of bacteria they are.

bacteriologist is a [microbiologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiologist), or similarly trained professional, in [bacteriology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteriology)— a subdivision of [microbiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiology) that studies [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria), typically [pathogenic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathogenic_bacteria) ones.

Bacteriology is the branch and specialty of [biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology) that studies the [morphology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphology_(biology)), [ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology), [genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) and [biochemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemistry) of [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) as well as many other aspects related to them.

biocide is defined in the European legislation as a [chemical substance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_substance) or [microorganism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microorganism) intended to destroy, deter, render harmless, or exert a controlling effect on any harmful organism.

Bioclogging or biological clogging refers to the blockage of [pore space in soil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pore_space_in_soil) by microbial biomass, including active cells and their byproducts such as [extracellular polymeric substance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extracellular_polymeric_substance) (EPS).

biofertilizer is a substance containing living [micro-organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micro-organism)s which, when applied to seeds, plant surfaces, or soil, colonize the [rhizosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhizosphere) or the interior of the [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant) and promote growth by increasing the supply or availability of primary [nutrient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nutrient)s to the host plant.

definition: Biogenic sulfide corrosion is a [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria)lly mediated process of forming [hydrogen sulfide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen_sulfide) gas and the subsequent conversion to [sulfuric acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sulfuric_acid) that attacks [concrete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concrete) and [steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steel) within [wastewater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wastewater) environments.

Biological carbon fixation, or carbon assimilation, is the [process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_process) by which living organisms convert [inorganic carbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_inorganic_carbon) (particularly [carbon dioxide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_dioxide), ) to [organic compound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organic_compound)s.

Biological Indicator Evaluation Resistometer (BIER) vessel is a piece of equipment used to determine the time taken to reduce survival of a given organism by 90% (also known as a [log 1 reduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Log_reduction)).

biological oxidizer is a device that uses [micro-organisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micro-organisms) to treat [wastewater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wastewater) and the [volatile organic compound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volatile_organic_compound)s produced by commercial and industrial operations.

Biological Stain Commission (BSC) is an organization that provides third-party testing and certification of [dye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dye)s and a few other compounds that are used to enhance contrast in specimens examined in biological and medical laboratories.

Bioluminescent bacteria are [light-producing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioluminescence) [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) that are predominantly present in sea water, marine sediments, the surface of decomposing fish and in the gut of marine animals.
Biomining refers to processes that use organisms to extract metals from [ore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ore)s and other solid materials.

Bioremediation of PCBs is the use of [microorganisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microorganism) to degrade PCBs from contaminated sites, relying on multiple microorganisms' co-metabolism.

biovar is a variant [prokaryotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prokaryotic) [strain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strain_(biology)) that differs physiologically or biochemically from other strains in a particular species.

definition: Cloacibacterium normanense is a bacterium originally found in wastewater in [Norman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norman,_Oklahoma), [Oklahoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma).

clonal colony or genet is a group of [genetically](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) identical individuals, such as [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s, [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi), or [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria), that have grown in a given location, all originating [vegetatively](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vegetative_reproduction), not [sexually](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_reproduction), from a single ancestor.
clonogenic assay is a cell biology technique for studying the effectiveness of specific agents on the survival and proliferation of cells.

Metaproteomics (also community proteomics, environmental proteomics, or community proteogenomics) is an umbrella term for experimental approaches to study all [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein)s in microbial communities and [microbiome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiome)s from [environmental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_environment) sources.

Metatranscriptomics is the set of techniques used to study [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) expression of [microbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbes) within natural environments, i.e., the metatranscriptome.

Methanogens are anaerobic [archaea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaea) that produce [methane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methane) as a byproduct of their energy [metabolism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metabolism), i.e., [catabolism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catabolism).

definition: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is a group of [Staphylococcus aureus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staphylococcus_aureus) strains that are [resistant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antimicrobial_resistance) to [β-lactam antibiotics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beta-lactam_antibiotics).
Methylarcula is a [genus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genus) of [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) in the family [Rhodobacteraceae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodobacteraceae).

Methylibium petroleiphilum is a species of [methyl tert-butyl ether](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methyl_tert-butyl_ether)-degrading [methylotroph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methylotroph), the type species of its genus.
Methylobacter tundripaludum is a [methane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methane)-oxidizing bacterium isolated in July 1996 from a wetland soil sampled near Ny-Ålesund, Svalbard.
Methylobacterium ajmalii is a species of [Methylobacterium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methylobacterium).

Methylobacterium nodulans is an aerobic, facultatively [methylotrophic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methylotrophic), [legume](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legume) [root nodule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Root_nodule)-forming and [nitrogen-fixing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nitrogen_fixation) bacteria.
Methylocapsa acidiphila is a bacterium.
Methylocella palustris is a species of bacterium.
Methylocella silvestris is a bacterium from the genus [Methylocella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methylocella) which are found in many acidic soils and wetlands.
Methylocella tundrae is a species of bacterium.

Methylomonas scandinavica is a species of [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative) [gammaproteobacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gammaproteobacteria) found in deep [igneous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igneous) rock ground water in [Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden).

Methylophaga marina is an obligately [methylotrophic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methylotrophic), [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative), strictly aerobic, [motile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motile), rod-shaped bacteria, the type species of its genus.

Methylophaga sulfidovorans is an obligately [methylotrophic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methylotrophic), aerobic, [dimethylsulfide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimethylsulfide)-oxidizing bacterium.

Methylophaga thalassica is an obligately [methylotrophic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methylotrophic), [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative), strictly aerobic, [motile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motile), rod-shaped bacteria.

Methylotrophs are a diverse group of [microorganism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microorganism)s that can use [reduced](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redox) one-carbon compounds, such as [methanol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methanol) or [methane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methane), as the carbon source for their growth; and multi-carbon compounds that contain no carbon-carbon bonds, such as [dimethyl ether](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimethyl_ether) and [dimethylamine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimethylamine).

definition: MicrobeLibrary is a permanent collection of over 1400 original peer-reviewed resources for teaching undergraduate [microbiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiology).

Microbial biodegradation is the use of [bioremediation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioremediation) and [biotransformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biotransformation) methods to harness the naturally occurring ability of microbial [xenobiotic metabolism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xenobiotic_metabolism) to degrade, transform or accumulate environmental pollutants, including [hydrocarbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrocarbon)s (e.g.
Microbial biogeography is a subset of [biogeography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biogeography), a field that concerns the distribution of organisms across space and time.

microbial consortium or microbial community, is two or more [bacterial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacterial) or [microbial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbial) groups living [symbiotically](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbiosis).
Microbial Culture Collection (now called the National Centre for Microbial Resource, NCMR) is a microbial culture collection centre in [Pune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pune), India.

microbial cyst is a resting or [dormant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dormancy) stage of a [microorganism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microorganism), that can be thought of as a state of [suspended animation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suspended_animation) in which the [metabolic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metabolism) processes of the cell are slowed and the cell ceases all activities like feeding and locomotion.
Microbial cytology is the study of microscopic and submicroscopic details of [microorganism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microorganism)s.

Microbial dark matter (MDM) comprises the vast majority of [microbial organisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbial_organism) (usually [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) and [archaea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaea)) that [microbiologists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiologists) are unable to [culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiological_culture) in the laboratory, due to lack of knowledge or ability to supply the required growth conditions.

microbial food web describes the network of [trophic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trophic_level) interactions among [microorganism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbe)s in aquatic ecosystems, including [viruses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viruses), [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria), [algae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algae), and heterotrophic [protists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protists) (such as [ciliates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciliates) and [flagellates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flagellates)).
Microbial genetics is a subject area within [microbiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiology) and [genetic engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_engineering).

Microbial inoculants, also known as soil inoculants or bioinoculants, are agricultural amendments that use beneficial [rhizosphericic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhizosphere) or [endophytic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endophytic) [microbe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbe)s to promote plant health.
Microbial intelligence (known as bacterial intelligence) is the [intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligence) shown by [microorganism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microorganism)s.

microbial loop describes a trophic pathway where, in aquatic systems, [dissolved organic carbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dissolved_organic_carbon) (DOC) is returned to higher trophic levels via its incorporation into bacterial biomass, and then coupled with the classic food chain formed by [phytoplankton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phytoplankton)-[zooplankton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zooplankton)-[nekton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nekton).

microbial mat is a multi-layered sheet or [biofilm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biofilm) of [microbial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbial) [colonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colony_(biology)), composed of mainly [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) and/or [archaea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaea).

Microbial pathogenesis is a field of [microbiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiology) that started at least as early as 1988, with the identification of the triune [Falkow's criteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falkow's_criteria), aka [molecular Koch's postulates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_Koch's_postulates).
Microbial phylogenetics is the study of the manner in which various groups of [microorganism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microorganism)s are genetically related.

Microbial population biology is the application of the principles of [population biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_biology) to [microorganisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microorganisms).

Microbial synergy is a phenomenon in which [aerobic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerobic_microbe) and [anaerobic microbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anaerobic_organism) support each other's growth and proliferation.

Microbiofuels are [biofuel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biofuel)s produced by microorganisms like [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria), [cyanobacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyanobacteria), [microalgae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algae_biofuel), fungi, etc.

microbiological culture, or microbial culture, is a method of multiplying [microbial organisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microorganism) by letting them reproduce in predetermined [culture medium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_medium) under controlled laboratory conditions.

definition: Microbiological Research is an [academic journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_journal) in [microbiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiology), published by [Elsevier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elsevier).

microbiologist (from [Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Greek) ) is a [scientist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientist) who studies [microscopic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microscopic) life forms and processes.

Microbiology is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that covers research in all aspects of [microbiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiology), including [biochemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemistry), [cell biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_biology), [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology), [developmental biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developmental_biology), [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology), [pathogenicity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathogenicity), [biodiversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodiversity), [biotechnology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biotechnology), [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution), and [genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) of [microorganism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microorganism)s and their [virus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virus)es.

Microbiology () is the [scientific study](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Branches_of_science) of [microorganisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microorganisms), those being of [unicellular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unicellular_organism) (single-celled), [multicellular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multicellular_organism) (consisting of complex cells), or [acellular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-cellular_life) (lacking cells).
related: International Journal of Systematic and Evolutionary Microbiology

definition: microbiology analyzer refers to the automated systems used in [microbiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiology) for [microbial identification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbial_identification) (ID) and [antibiotic sensitivity testing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antibiotic_sensitivity_testing) (AST).

Microbiology and Molecular Biology Reviews (published as MMBR) is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) published by the [American Society for Microbiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Society_for_Microbiology).
categories: American Society for Microbiology academic journals

definition: Microbiology of decomposition is the study of all microorganisms involved in [decomposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decomposition), the chemical and physical processes during which organic matter is broken down and reduced to its original elements.

Microbiology Outreach Prize is awarded annually by the [Microbiology Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiology_Society) to those who made outstanding innovation in outreach about microbiology.

[Fleming Prize Lecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fleming_Prize_Lecture) is awarded annually to recognise outstanding research in any branch of microbiology by a microbiologist in the early stages of his/her career.

Microbiology Society Prize Medal is awarded annually by the [Microbiology Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiology_Society) to those who have made an impact beyond microbiology and are world leaders in their field.

Microbiology Spectrum is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) published by the [American Society for Microbiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Society_for_Microbiology).

microorganism, or microbe, is an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism) of [microscopic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microscopic_scale) size, which may exist in its [single-celled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unicellular_organism) form or as a [[Colony (biology)#Microbial colonies|colony of cells]].

Micropollutants are substances that even at very low concentrations have adverse effects on different environmental matrices.

microscope () is a [laboratory instrument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laboratory_equipment) used to examine objects that are too small to be seen by the [naked eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naked_eye).

Microscopy is the technical field of using [microscope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microscope)s to view subjects too small to be seen with the [naked eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naked_eye) (objects that are not within the resolution range of the normal eye).
Microtechnique is an aggregate of methods used to prepare micro-objects for studying.

Milnesium alpigenum is a [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) of [tardigrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tardigrade) that falls under the [Tardigrada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tardigrade) [phylum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylum).

Mineral salts pyridine broth is a [selective medium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selective_medium) for [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacterium) that can [metabolize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metabolism) [pyridine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyridine) (which is an unusual [carbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon) source that a select few types of bacteria can use).
minicells are bacterial cells that are smaller than usual.

minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) is the lowest concentration of a [chemical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical), usually a drug, which prevents visible [in vitro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_vitro) [growth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_growth) of [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) or [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus).

Molecular Microbiology is a bimonthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering all aspects of [molecular microbiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_microbiology).
monokaryon is a fungal [mycelium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mycelium) or [hypha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypha) in which each cell contains a single nucleus.

definition: Tannerella forsythia is an [anaerobic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anaerobic_organism), [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative) bacterial species of the [Bacteroidota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteroidota) phylum.
Tatumella ptyseos is a species of [gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative_bacteria) bacteria first isolated from human clinical specimens, predominantly sputum.

taxon in disguise is a [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species), [genus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genus) or higher unit of [biological classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_classification) whose evolutionary history reveals that it has evolved from another unit of a similar or lower rank, making the parent unit [paraphyletic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paraphyly).

Taylorella equigenitalis is a [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative), non-motile, microaerophilic [bacterium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacterium) of the genus [Taylorella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylorella), and the causative agent of [contagious equine metritis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contagious_equine_metritis) (CEM) in horses.

Teliospore (sometimes called teleutospore) is the thick-walled [resting spore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resting_spore) of some [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi) ([rusts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(fungus)) and [smuts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smut_(fungus))), from which the [basidium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basidium) arises.

temperate refers to the ability of some [bacteriophages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteriophages) (notably [coliphage λ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambda_phage)) to display a [lysogenic life cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lysogenic_life_cycle).
Tenacibaculum adriaticum is a species of [gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative_bacteria) bacterium.
Tenacibaculum lutimaris is a bacterium.
Tenacibaculum skagerrakense is a bacterium.
Tenacibaculum soleae is a species of bacterium from the order [Flavobacteriales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavobacteriales).
Tepidibacter mesophilus is a bacterium from the family [Peptostreptococcaceae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peptostreptococcaceae).
Tepidibacter thalassicus is a bacterium from the family [Peptostreptococcaceae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peptostreptococcaceae).
Tepidisphaeraceae is a family of [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria).
Tetraspora gelatinosa is a species of [green algae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_algae).
Tetratrichomonas undula is a species of [parabasalid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parabasalid).

Thalassionema nitzschioides is a type of [phytoplankton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phytoplankton) belonging to the [pennate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennales) [diatom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diatom) group.
Thalassobaculaceae is a family of [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) from the order [Rhodospirillales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodospirillales).
Thalassolituus marinus is a gram negative, rod shaped, motile, hydrocarbon utilizing marine bacterium.
Thalassolituus oleivorans is a species of bacteria, the type species of its genus.
Thalassospiraceae is a family of [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) from the order [Rhodospirillales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodospirillales).
Thanatophages, are organisms that obtain [nutrient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nutrient)s by consuming decomposing dead plant biomass.

Thauera is a genus of [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative) [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacterium) in the family [Zoogloeaceae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoogloeaceae) of the order [Rhodocyclales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodocyclales) of the [Betaproteobacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betaproteobacteria).
Thauera aromatica is a species of bacteria.

The ISME Journal: Multidisciplinary Journal of Microbial Ecology is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that covers diverse and integrated areas of [microbial ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbial_ecology) spanning the breadth of microbial life, including [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria), [archaea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaea), microbial [eukaryotes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryotes), and [virus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virus)es.

The Journal of Antibiotics is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [medical journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_journal) published by the [Nature Publishing Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nature_Publishing_Group) for the [Japan Antibiotics Research Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan_Antibiotics_Research_Association).

The Journal of Infectious Diseases is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) biweekly [medical journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_journal) published by [Oxford University Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_University_Press) on behalf of the [Infectious Diseases Society of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infectious_Diseases_Society_of_America).

The Lichenologist is a bimonthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) specialising in [lichenology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lichenology), including [taxonomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxonomy_(biology)), [systematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systematics), [ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology), [biogeography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biogeography), and [conservation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservation_biology).

Thecamoeba homeri is a [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) of [amoebae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amoebae) belonging to the [phylum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylum) [Amoebozoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amoebozoa).

Thermanaeromonas toyohensis is a species of [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) within the family [Thermoanaerobacteraceae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermoanaerobacteraceae).

Thermoanaerobacter siderophilus is a [dissimilatory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dissimilatory_metal-reducing_microorganisms) [Fe(III)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron)-reducing, [anaerobic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anaerobic_organism), [thermophilic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermophilic) bacterium that was firstly isolated from the sediment of a [hydrothermal vent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrothermal_vent) found near the [Karymsky volcano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karymsky_(volcano)), in the [Kamchatka peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamchatka_peninsula), Russia.
Thermoanaerobacter thermocopriae, previously known as Clostridium thermocopriae is a bacterium belonging to the [Bacillota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacillota).

Thermoanaerobacterium aotearoense is a slightly [acidophilic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acidophilic), [anaerobic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anaerobic_organism), [thermophile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermophile) first isolated from hot springs in New Zealand, hence its name.
Thermocrinis minervae is a bacterium.

Thermocrinis ruber is a species of [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative_bacteria) bacteria first discovered in Octopus Spring in [Yellowstone National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellowstone_National_Park).
Thermodesulfobacterium commune is a species of [sulfate-reducing bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sulfate-reducing_bacteria).

Thermodesulfobacterium hveragerdense is a bacterial species belonging to genus [Thermodesulfobacterium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermodesulfobacterium), which are thermophilic sulfate-reducing bacteria.
Thermodesulfobacterium hydrogeniphilum is a species of [Sulfate-reducing bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sulfate-reducing_bacteria).

Thermodesulfobiaceae according to the [LPSN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Prokaryotic_names_with_Standing_in_Nomenclature) is located within the order [Thermoanaerobacterales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermoanaerobacterales) and class [Clostridia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clostridia).

Thermodesulforhabdus norvegica is a species of [thermophilic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermophilic) [sulfate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sulfate)-reducing bacteria, the type and only species of its genus.
Thermodesulfovibrio aggregans is a species of bacterium.
Thermoguttaceae is a family of [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria).

Thermoleophilum album is a bacterium obligate for [thermophily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermophily) and [n-alkane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N-alkane) substrates, the type species of its genus.

Thermosinus carboxydivorans is an anaerobic, [thermophilic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermophilic), [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative), [carbon-monoxide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_monoxide)-oxidizing, [hydrogenogenic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogenogenic) bacterium, the type species of its genus.

Thermosyntropha lipolytica is a [lipolytic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lipolytic), anaerobic, [alkalitolerant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alkalitolerant), [thermophilic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermophilic) bacteria.
Thermotoga elfii is a [rod-shaped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacillus_(shape)), glucose-[fermenting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermentation) bacterium.
Thermotoga hypogea is a hyperthermophilic organism that is a member of the order [Thermotogales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermotogales).

Thermotoga lettingae is a [thermophilic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermophilic), anaerobic, non-[spore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spore)-forming, [motile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motile) and [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative) bacterium, with type strain TMO ==References== ==Further reading== *Dworkin, Martin, and Stanley Falkow, eds.

Thioalkalivibrio denitrificancs is an obligately [alkaliphilic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alkaliphilic) and obligately [chemolithoautotrophic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemolithoautotrophic) sulfur-oxidizing bacteria.

Thioalkalivibrio nitratis is an obligately [alkaliphilic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alkaliphilic) and obligately [chemolithoautotrophic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemolithoautotrophic) sulfur-oxidizing bacteria.

Thioalkalivibrio thiocyanoxidans is a species of [alkaliphilic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alkaliphilic) and obligately [autotrophic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autotrophic) sulfur-oxidizing bacterium.

Thioalkalivibrio versutus is an obligately [alkaliphilic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alkaliphilic) and obligately [chemolithoautotrophic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemolithoautotrophic) sulfur-oxidizing bacteria.

Thiorhodovibrio winogradskyi is a [purple sulfur bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purple_sulfur_bacteria), the type species of its genus.

Thiosocius is a genus of [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) that lives in symbiosis with the giant [shipworm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shipworms) [Kuphus polythalamius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuphus_polythalamius).

Thiosulfate–citrate–bile salts–sucrose agar, or TCBS agar, is a type of selective [agar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agar) culture plate that is used in [microbiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiology) [laboratories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laboratories) to isolate [Vibrio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vibrio) species.

Tisochrysis lutea is a species of [Haptophyta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haptophyta) formerly known as [Isochrysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isochrysis) affinis galbana (Tahiti isolate) or 'T-iso'.

Tissue tropism is the range of cells and tissues of a [host](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Host_(biology)) that support growth of a particular [pathogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathogen), such as a [virus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virus_(biology)), [bacterium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) or [parasite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasite).

Titia de Lange (born 11 November 1955, in [Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam)) is the Director of the Anderson Center for Cancer Research, the Leon Hess professor and the head of Laboratory Cell Biology and Genetics at [Rockefeller University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockefeller_University).

Totally drug-resistant tuberculosis (TDR-TB) is a generic term for [tuberculosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuberculosis) strains that are resistant to a wider range of drugs than strains classified as [extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extensively_drug-resistant_tuberculosis).

Treponema azotonutricium is a bacterium, the first termite gut [spirochete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirochete) to be isolated, together with [Treponema primitia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treponema_primitia).
Treponema isoptericolens is a spirochaete from the hindgut of the termite [Incisitermes tabogae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incisitermes_tabogae).

Trichia crateriformis is a [slime mold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slime_mold) [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) in the [order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_(biology)) [Trichiida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trichiida) found in temperate areas throughout the world.

Trichodesmium thiebautii is a [cyanobacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyanobacteria) that is often found in open oceans of tropical and subtropical regions and is known to be a contributor to large oceanic [surface blooms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algal_bloom).

Tripartite motif-containing protein 5 also known as RING finger protein 88 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the TRIM5 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Trinickia caryophylli is a gram-negative, motile, parasitic bacteria.

Trinidad Regional Virus Laboratory (T.R.V.L.) was established in [Port of Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Spain), in 1953 by the [Rockefeller Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockefeller_Foundation) in co-operation with the Government of [Trinidad and Tobago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinidad_and_Tobago).

Truepera is the only genus of [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) in the family [Trueperaceae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trueperaceae) from the phylum [Deinococcota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deinococcota).

Trypanosoma rangeli is a species of [hemoflagellate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemoflagellate) excavate parasites of the genus [Trypanosoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trypanosoma).

Trypanosoma suis is a species of excavate [trypanosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trypanosomatid) in the genus [Trypanosoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trypanosoma) that causes one form of the [surra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surra) disease in animals.

Tryptic soy broth or Trypticase soy broth (frequently abbreviated as TSB) is used in [microbiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiology) laboratories as a culture broth to grow [aerobic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerobic_organism) and [facultative anaerobic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facultative_anaerobic_organism) [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria).

Trypticase soy agar or Tryptic soy agar (TSA) is a [growth media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Growth_medium) for the [culturing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiological_culture) of moderately to non [fastidious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fastidious_organism) [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria).

Triple Sugar Iron (TSI) test is a [microbiological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiological) test roughly named for its ability to test a microorganism's ability to ferment sugars and to produce [hydrogen sulfide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen_sulfide).
Tumebacillus algifaecis is a species of [Gram positive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram_positive), facultatively anaerobic, [bacterium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacterium).
Tumebacillus avium is a species of [Gram positive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram_positive), facultatively aerobic, [bacterium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacterium).
Tumebacillus flagellatus is a species of [Gram positive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram_positive), aerobic, [bacterium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacterium).
Tumebacillus ginsengisoli is a species of [Gram positive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram_positive), aerobic, [bacterium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacterium).
Tumebacillus lipolyticus is a species of [Gram positive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram_positive), aerobic, [bacterium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacterium).
Tumebacillus luteolus is a species of [Gram positive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram_positive), aerobic, [bacterium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacterium).
Tumebacillus permanentifrigorisis is a species of [Gram positive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram_positive), strictly aerobic, [bacterium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacterium).
Tumebacillus soli is a species of [Gram positive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram_positive), aerobic, [bacterium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacterium).

Tumor-homing bacteria are [facultative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facultative_anaerobic_organism) or [obligate anaerobic bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obligate_anaerobe) (capable of producing ATP when oxygen is absent or is destroyed in normal oxygen levels) that are able to target [cancerous cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cancer_cell) in the body, suppress tumor growth and survive in the body for a long time even after the infection.
Twitching motility is a form of crawling bacterial motility used to move over surfaces.

Xylella fastidiosa is an aerobic, [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative_bacterium) bacterium of the genus [Xylella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xylella).

categories: Fellows of the American Academy of Microbiology
related: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases

definition: Yasuko Rikihisa is a veterinary microbiologist known for research on obligate intracellular bacteria, especially species in the genera [Ehrlichia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ehrlichia), [Anaplasma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anaplasma), and [Neorickettsia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neorickettsia).
categories: Fellows of the American Academy of Microbiology

definition: Yeast is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) published by [Wiley-Blackwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiley-Blackwell).

yeast in winemaking is the most important element that distinguishes [wine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wine) from [fruit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fruit) [juice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice).

definition: Yeosuana aromativorans is a [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) of non-motile [aerobic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerobic_organism) [marine bacterium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_bacterium) that can degrade [benzopyrene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benzopyrene).
YEPD or yeast extract peptone dextrose, also often abbreviated as YPD, is a complete [medium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Growth_medium) for [yeast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yeast) growth.
Yersinia is a [genus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genus) of [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) in the family [Yersiniaceae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yersiniaceae).
Yersinia aldovae is a species of bacteria that was originally described as Group X2 [Yersinia enterocolitica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yersinia_enterocolitica).

Yersinia alsatica is a [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative) bacterium in the family [Yersiniaceae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yersiniaceae) that has been isolated from [human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human) stool.

Yersinia artesiana are short [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative) rod [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) in the [Yersiniaceae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yersiniaceae) family that have been isolated from [human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human) stool.
Yersinia bercovieri is a [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative) species of [enteric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enteric) bacteria.

Yersinia canariae is a [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative) species of [Yersinia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yersinia) that was isolated from a [human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human) displaying symptoms of [yersiniosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yersiniosis).

Yersinia entomophaga is a species of bacteria that was originally isolated from the diseased [larvae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larvae) of the [New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand) grass grub, [Costelytra zealandica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costelytra_zealandica).
Yersinia frederiksenii is a [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative) species of bacteria.
Yersinia hibernica is a species of [Yersinia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yersinia) that was originally isolated in a [pig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pig)-production environment.

Yersinia intermedia is a [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative) species of bacteria submit=Search Type strain of Yersinia intermedia at BacDive - the Bacterial Diversity Metadatabase] [[Category:Yersinia|intermedia]] [[Category:Bacteria described in 1980]] 3t3esbz6cvgiel7ntdo1eltercqfaih
Yersinia kristensenii is a species of bacteria.
Yersinia massiliensis is a [Gram-negative bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative_bacteria) that is commonly isolated from the environment and food.
Yersinia mollaretii is a [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative) species of bacteria.

Yersinia nurmii is a [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative) species of [Yersinia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yersinia) that was originally isolated in packaged broiler meat cuts.

Yersinia pekkanenii is a [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative) species of [Yersinia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yersinia) that has been isolated from [water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water), [soil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soil), and [lettuce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lettuce) samples.

Yersinia proxima is a [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative) bacterium in the family [Yersiniaceae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yersiniaceae) that is [phylogenetically](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylogenetically) close to [Yersinia enterocolitica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yersinia_enterocolitica).

Yersinia rochesterensis is a [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative), motile, rod-shaped bacterium that forms circular colonies and was isolated from [human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human) feces.

Yersinia rohdei is a [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative) species of [Yersinia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yersinia) that was originally isolated from the [feces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feces) of [humans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humans) and [dogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dogs) in addition to water surfaces.

Yersinia ruckeri is a species of [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative) [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria), known for causing [enteric redmouth disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enteric_redmouth_disease) in some species of fish.

Yersinia similis is a [Gram-negative bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative_bacteria) species of [Yersinia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yersinia) that resembles [Yersinia pseudotuberculosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yersinia_pseudotuberculosis) phenotypically but differs on the basis of [16S ribosomal RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/16S_ribosomal_RNA) sequences.

Yersinia thracica is a [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative) species of [enteric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enteric) bacteria in the [Yersinia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yersinia) genus that is closely related to [Yersinia kristensenii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yersinia_kristensenii).

Yersinia vastinensis is a [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative) species of [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) that has been isolated from [human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human) stools.

Yersinia wautersii is a species of [Gram-negative bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative_bacteria) that was originally called the Korean Group of the [Yersinia pseudotuberculosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yersinia_pseudotuberculosis) complex.

Yevgeny Nikanorovich Pavlovsky (; 5 March 1884, [Biryuch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biryuch) – 27 May 1965, [Leningrad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Petersburg)) was a [Soviet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union) zoologist, entomologist, academician of the [Academy of Sciences of the Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Sciences_of_the_Soviet_Union) (1939), the [Academy of Medical Sciences of the USSR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Medical_Sciences_of_the_USSR) (1944), honorary member of the [Tajik Academy of Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tajik_Academy_of_Sciences) (1951), and a [lieutenant general](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_general) of the [Red Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Army) Medical Service in [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II).
categories: Employees of the Gamaleya Research Institute of Epidemiology and Microbiology

definition: YM Agar and Broth, is a [selective](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selective_medium) [growth medium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Growth_medium) with low [pH](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PH) useful for cultivating [yeast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yeast)s, [mold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mold_(fungus))s, or other [acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acid)-tolerant or [acidophilic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acidophile) organisms, while deterring growth of most [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) and other acid intolerant organisms.
Yokenella is a [genus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genus) of [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) of the family [Enterobacteriaceae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enterobacteriaceae).

Zhenhengia is a genus of [Gram-positive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-positive) and [strictly anaerobic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obligate_anaerobe) bacteria in the family [Lachnospiraceae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lachnospiraceae).

Ziehl–Neelsen stain, also known as the acid-fast stain, is a bacteriological [staining](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staining) technique used in [cytopathology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytopathology) and [microbiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiology) to identify [acid-fast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acid-fastness) bacteria under [microscopy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microscopy), particularly members of the [Mycobacterium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mycobacterium) genus.

Zinaida Vissarionovna Yermolyeva (; – 2 December 1974) was a Soviet [microbiologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiologist) of Don Cossack origin most notable for producing [penicillin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penicillin) for the Soviet military during World War II.
categories: Employees of the Gamaleya Research Institute of Epidemiology and Microbiology

definition: Zixibacteria is a [bacterial phylum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacterial_phyla) with [candidate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candidatus) status, meaning it had no cultured representatives.

Zobellia galactanivorans is a [gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative_bacteria) [marine bacterium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_bacterium) isolated from the surface of [red algae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_algae) of the coast of [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France).

Zooflagellates are [single-celled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-celled) [eukaryote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryote)s with [flagella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flagella) (i.e., [flagellate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flagellate)s).

zoospore is a [motile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motility) asexual [spore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spore) that uses a [flagellum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flagellum) for [locomotion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motion_(physics)) in aqueous or moist environments.

zygospore is a [diploid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diploid) reproductive stage in the life cycle of many [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi) and [protist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protist)s.
Zymophilus paucivorans is a species of anaerobic, [Gram-negative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative), rod-shaped bacteria first isolated from spoilt beer.
